{{legend0|#F48882|Republican hold}} {{legend0|#CA0120|Republican gain}} | title = [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|Speaker]] | before_election = [[John Boehner]] | before_party = Republican Party (US) | after_election = [[John Boehner]] | after_party = Republican Party (US) }} The '''2014 United States House of Representatives elections''' were held on November 4, 2014, in the middle of President [[Barack Obama]]'s second term in office. Elections were held for all 435 seats of the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]], representing the 50 [[U.S. state|state]]s. Elections were also held for the [[Delegate (United States Congress)|non-voting delegates]] from the [[District of Columbia]] and four of the five [[Insular area|territories]]. The winners of these elections served in the [[114th United States Congress]], with seats apportioned among the states based on the [[2010 United States census]]. The Republicans won 16 seats from Democrats, while three Republican-held seats turned Democratic. The Republicans achieved their largest majority in the House since [[1928 United States House of Representatives elections|1928]] due to a sizeable Republican wave.[https://www.politico.com/magazine/story/2014/11/1928-congress-last-time-republicans-had-a-majority-this-huge-112913/ What Happened the Last Time Republicans Had a Majority This Huge?], Politico, November 15, 2014 Combined with the Republican gains made in [[2010 United States House of Representatives elections|2010]], the total number of Democratic-held House seats lost under [[Barack Obama]]'s presidency in [[United States midterm election|midterm elections]] rose to 77 with these elections. This marked the highest number of House seats lost under a two-term president of the same party since [[Harry S. Truman]].{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/republicans-match-post-wwii-record-after-holding-two-la-house-seats/ |title=Republicans match post-WWII record after holding two La. House seats |newspaper=[[Fox News Channel]] |date=December 7, 2014 |access-date=December 7, 2014}} With 36.4% of eligible voters voting, the [[voter turnout]] was the lowest since [[1942 United States House of Representatives elections|1942]].{{cite news |first1=Domenico|last1=Montanaro |first2=Rachel|last2=Wellford |first3=Simone|last3=Pathe |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/2014-midterm-election-turnout-lowest-in-70-years |title=2014 midterm election turnout lowest in 70 years |newspaper=[[PBS NewsHour]] |date=November 10, 2014 |access-date=August 30, 2015}} As of 2026, this is the last congressional election in which Democrats won a House seat in [[Nebraska]], the last time Republicans won a House seat in [[New Hampshire]], and the last time Republicans won more than one House seat in the [[New England]] region. == Results summary == === Federal === {| style="width:60em; text-align:center" |+ ↓ |- style="color:white" | style="background:{{party color|Democratic Party (US)}}; width:43.22%" | '''188''' | style="background:{{party color|Republican Party (US)}}; width:56.78%" | '''247''' |- | '''Democratic''' | '''Republican''' |} {| class=wikitable style="text-align:center" |- ! rowspan=2 colspan=2 | Parties ! colspan=4 | Seats ! colspan=3 | Popular vote |- style="background:#e9e9e9;" !
